name: Question 1
problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=6\sqrt{x}\,{y}^{2},\,y(1)=2
$$

Using the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx=1,$ the new value ${y}_{\text{new}}$ is obtained by solving the equation $g({y}_{\text{new}})=0$ at each step. Which of the following is the **general form** of $g({y}_{\text{new}})$ in terms of the new values ${x}_{\text{new}}$ and ${y}_{\text{new}},$ and the current values $x$ and $y?$

Consider the following initial value problem: y′=6xy2,y(1)=2 Using the trapezoidal method with step size Δx=1, the new value ynew is obtained by solving the equation g(ynew)=0 at each step. Which of the following is the general form of g(ynew) in terms of the new values xnew and ynew, and the current values x and y?

a
g(ynew)=ynew−3xnewynew3−y−3xy2
b
g(ynew)=ynew+3xnewynew2−y−3xy2
c
g(ynew)=ynew−6xnewynew2−y−6xy2
d
g(ynew)=ynew−3xnewynew2−y−3xnewy2
e
g(ynew)=ynew−3xnewynew2−y−3xy2
